body: which-round-clears-a-round-level-test-entry: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:standing_entries (L3295-L3306) and tests:entry_cleared (L3287-L3291) decide when a round-level entry (leftovers--<kind>, stopped--silence, schedule--<a>--<b>) stops standing. The filed problem has partly rotted: the built rule is not 'any concerned test' everywhere. An entry from a whole-suite round clears once a later closed round reaches ANY test it concerns; an entry from a rerun round, and every schedule-- entry, clears only once a later closed round reaches EVERY test it concerns (needs_every = rerun or schedule). A test counts as reached where the later round recorded a result for it that is not not_run. tests:entry_tests (L3280-L3285) sets the concerned tests: both tests of a schedule pair, the round's unreached tests for a stop, the round's planned tests for leftovers. Separately, a new closed whole-suite round drops every entry from earlier rounds (standing_entries skips rounds before tests:latest_whole) and then carries its own entries. Mechanism: tests failures, tests reports, tests settled, and review certified all read standing_entries, so the rule decides when certification may close. Corpus: silent on which round clears a round-level entry. decision:fixes-rerun-the-tests-they-reach says only 'A standing result that outlives its round keeps a failure in view until a later run passes it' (per-test results, not round entries). decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests says each grown leftover count files a report and the loop repeats 'until a whole-suite round passes after the last change'. decision:tests-isolated-unless-declared: 'Counting leftovers each round catches a leak in the round that made it.' No clause names the clearing evidence. Harm: none an entry covers today; this is a product-intent choice about what evidence settles a round failure. Options: A, keep what is built (whole-round entries cleared by a later round reaching any concerned test, rerun and schedule entries by one reaching all), and write it into decision:fixes-rerun-the-tests-they-reach; cost: a narrow rerun that touches one planned test clears a whole round's leftover entry though most of the round's tests never ran again. B, only a round whose tests match the fixed defect's own test list clears it; cost: the tests tool must tie a rerun round to a defect, which the results file does not record today. C, only the next closed whole-suite round clears a round-level entry; cost: every fix of a leftover, stop, or schedule failure waits a full suite round, though decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests already ends certification on a passing whole-suite round. D (filer missed): one rule for every entry kind, a later closed round that reaches every test the entry concerns; cost: a whole-round leftover entry then needs a rerun of every planned test, close to C. Recommendation leans A or C: A matches the code; C matches the gate the loop already requires. No sibling issues.

body: planned-story-with-no-scenario-offered-as-untested: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:offer_groups (L908-929) builds the untested group from stories 'not in recorded and slug not in state["stamps"] and slug not in answered', and the stale group from every story with recorded scenarios or a stamp whose blob differs (L917-923). So a story a plan stamped with no scenario leaves the untested offer and turns stale when its file changes. The filed problem holds. Mechanism: the archive step (tests:cmd_stamp, L4708ff) stamps each planned story whose every planned scenario was written, kept, or retired; a story planned with zero scenarios passes that test vacuously and gets a stamp. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once defines 'A story is untested where it has no recorded scenario and no recorded answer that leaves it unguarded, and stale where its file's blob id differs from its test stamp' -- read literally, the stamp plays no part in 'untested', so the built code departs from that sentence (the filer missed this); its rationale says a story that loses its stamp 'reads as untested or stale'. decision:tests-check-scenarios: a scenario no code supports 'is a gap, recorded with no test', and 'A program no story serves gets no test: the owner either asks a sprint for the story it serves or records it as unguarded' -- unguarded is the owner's answer for programs, silent on planned stories. decision:testing-runs-inside-the-sprint lists untested and stale as offer groups. Harm: none an accept-list entry covers today; this is what the product commits to. Options: A. Amend the untested definition so a test stamp also removes a story from untested (what is built); cost: the corpus sentence changes, and a story whose plan found nothing testable comes back only as stale when its file changes. B. A plan records each planned story it left with no scenario as unguarded, with a reason; cost: the entry never clears when the story's file changes, so a changed story hides from every later offer until the owner clears it, and the plan gains a write. C (the filer missed it).
